To: d.kerrigan@northmail.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: none
Subject: Re: Blister packs for my mother - new patient

Dear Mr Kerrigan,

Thank you for getting in touch. I’m sorry to hear about your mother’s fall, and I hope she is recovering well. We’d be happy to help Margaret get settled at home with a safer, more organised medication routine.

We prepare weekly blister packs, with doses organised four times a day. There is no charge for the packaging itself; Margaret would pay the usual dispensing costs, with most eligible prescription costs covered by the Ontario Drug Benefit program. We can deliver to her building on our Tuesday and Friday delivery routes between 2 and 6 p.m. Delivery is free within 8 km, and her building is within our service area. For her first pack, we can arrange pickup or, if more convenient, a one-time Saturday delivery before 1 p.m.

To transfer her prescriptions, please send us the name and address of her current pharmacy and Margaret’s OHIP number. With that information, we can contact the pharmacy directly; she does not need to sign a transfer form. Please also ask the hospital to fax her discharge prescriptions to us as early as possible on Thursday morning. We need all prescriptions, including the discharge prescriptions and transfers, before we can prepare the packs. Once everything is received, we need about 48 hours, so we expect the first packs could be ready Saturday.

The first packs won’t be ready at the time of discharge on Thursday. Please ask the discharge team to confirm that Margaret will have enough medication to cover the period until Saturday, and to explain how she should take each dose in the meantime. It would be helpful if you can support her with every dose until she can start using the packs, whether you arrange pickup or delivery on Saturday.

I understand it may be easier for you to discuss the medications on Margaret’s behalf. Before we can discuss her medication information with you, however, we need Margaret’s permission. We use a signed Family Communication Consent form to record that permission. This is a routine privacy safeguard that helps ensure we only share her personal health information with people she has authorized. She can sign the form when the packs are picked up, or we can send it with the driver.

After discharge, I’d also be glad to complete a 20-minute MedsCheck with Margaret, either in person at the pharmacy or at her home if she is not mobile. I can visit Monday or Tuesday after 6 p.m. during the first week she is home. Let me know which evening would work best.

You can reach me directly at 905-555-0148, extension 2. I’m in the store Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. I look forward to helping Margaret and your family through the transition.

Kind regards,

Rania Haddad, Pharmacist
Erindale Park Pharmacy
